narrative_passages.title: 'Ad, Thamud and Pharaoh
narrative_passages.treatment_reason: Read only; no one is shown.

summary_for_children: Al-Fajr means The Dawn. It recalls 'Ad, Thamud and Pharaoh who oppressed, and teaches caring for orphans and the poor.
world_title: The Dawn and the Pillars of Iram
environment_concept: A dawn lookout (89:1). Further on, the weathered ruins of very tall pillars for Iram, who had lofty pillars (89:7), and a valley where doorways are carved into the rock for Thamud (89:9). Both are artistic stand-ins, empty and quiet, not the real places. No person is shown; the punishment of 89:13 and the Day of 89:21-26 are not pictured.
architecture_and_scenery: A lookout with seats, tall broken pillars on a platform, a rock valley with carved doorways.

unique_world.visual_theme: A palm grove at first light with baskets of dates on a mat, two small bowls, and a basket by the gate

primary_mechanic.text: Share four baskets of dates (12, 9, 7, 10) between two orphan sisters by pairing them one for each; then say even (none left) or odd (one left, which goes to the poor family); declaring before pairing is done is refused, and a wrong answer is noted (89:3 the even and the odd; 89:17-18 honour the orphan, feed the poor).

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading on the path, sharing the dates, then a reading among the palms
environment_behaviour: the sisters’ bowls fill as baskets are shared
odd dates gather in the gate basket
unique_world.learning_objective: Honour the orphan and urge feeding the poor (89:17-18)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Dawn and the Ancient Peoples
story_library.children_narration: The surah begins with an oath by dawn and recalls powerful ancient communities, including 'Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh. It reminds us not to become proud because of wealth or strength and encourages care for orphans and the poor.

world_idea.title: The Dawn Archaeological Expedition
world_idea.description: Travel through three distinct historical-style regions and discover lessons about power, generosity, and responsibility.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The library speaks of "historical regions". Iram, Thamud and Pharaoh's places are labelled as imagined, not reconstructed.
